title: Prove the realizable two-plane signatures of 4x4 bases are exactly 439 (no κ)
body:
## Result

Scoped proof with exact finite corroboration. **No new κ**; the selected result, the selected suppliers and `upstream/` are unchanged. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

In the two-plane, four-message model of #3997, the plane-level signature of an invertible 4x4 matrix over any field depends only on two complementary 2-planes of K^4: the row spaces of its top and bottom port pairs. Sources test whether a plane lies in a coordinate hyperplane. Readers test whether a coordinate vector lies in the *other* plane. Three necessary conditions follow (C1 to C3). They leave exactly **439** of the 6,561 candidate signatures, and over Q every one of the 439 is realized by an explicit integer matrix with entries in {-1, 0, 1}. These 439 are exactly the signature codes that #3997 records in `TERNARY-SCREEN.txt`. So rational values outside {-1, 0, 1}, through exact cofactor cancellations, add no signature to the generic and ternary censuses. This answers the signature question left open in #3997's `TASK.json`.

Not new: the invoice consequence (minimum copy invoice 8 on all 1,540 plane pairs for every invertible basis) agrees with, and is weaker than, #4365. That merged package proves COPY mass 8 for any finite scalar factorization on two matched planes, over every field. This PR claims only the classification of signatures.

Claim type: scoped written proof (`PROOF.md`) with exact finite corroboration. It is not a complete multiplication theorem, a supplier, or a search failure.

## Evidence

All counts come from `research/two-plane-signature-classes/verify.py`, which regenerates `RESULT.json` and `WITNESSES.json` and compares their bytes.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Candidate signatures | 9^4 = 6,561 |
| Pass C1, C2 and C3 | 439 |
| Pass two of the three (without C1 / C2 / C3) | 555 / 805 / 1,771 |
| Equal to the 439 codes in #3997's `TERNARY-SCREEN.txt` | yes |
| Distinct planes spanned by two ternary vectors | 362; all their complementary pairs give signatures in the 439 |
| Integer witnesses, each checked by exact rational inversion | 439 |
| F_2: planes / complementary pairs / signatures | 35 / 560 / 355 |
| F_3: planes / complementary pairs / signatures | 130 / 10,530 / 439 |
| F_5: planes / complementary pairs / signatures | 806 / 503,750 / 439 |
| F_7 (opt-in `--extended`): planes / pairs / signatures | 2,850 / 6,842,850 / 439 |
| Plane rule vs direct matrix inversion | all pairs at F_2 and F_3; 8,258 at F_5 (every 61st); 6,863 at F_7 (every 997th) |
| Direct census of every matrix of GL_4(F_2) | 20,160 matrices, the same 355 signatures |
| Rejection controls | 11 |

The finite-field enumerations corroborate Lemma 1; the proof does not use them.

## Reproduce

Interpreter: `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12` (CPython 3.12.15). From the repository root, on head `e68cb25dcc859efb03d616305f543fda2d90ece1`:

```sh
PY=~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12
$PY -I -B research/two-plane-signature-classes/verify.py
$PY -I -O -B research/two-plane-signature-classes/verify.py
$PY -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-plane-signature-classes --check-only
$PY -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-plane-signature-classes
$PY -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/two-plane-signature-classes --check-source-history
$PY -I -B research/two-plane-signature-classes/verify.py --extended   # opt-in, adds F_7
```

Local results: each `verify.py` run prints `PASS_TWO_PLANE_SIGNATURE_CLASSES` in about 1.4 s; the registered replay prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed` in about 3 s (both registered commands); the committed-bytes and source-history check prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`; the opt-in F_7 run takes about 13 s. Every registered check is far under the CI limit.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- Plane-level signatures only. The finer joint zero pattern of P and P^-1 (the cofactor strata of the original question) is not classified. It is not needed for the invoice.
- The invoice consequence relies on #3997's definition of the pricing (a function of the signature) and its recorded minimum; neither is recomputed here. The invoice floor itself is #4365's theorem.
- Two planes of two ports and four messages. Three or more planes, overcomplete factorizations, coefficient scaling cost, physical routing and restoration are outside scope, as in #3997.
- The proof is a written argument, not machine-checked. No independent human or formal proof-kernel review is claimed.
- Over F_2 only 355 of the 439 signatures occur. "The realizable set is the 439" is a statement about Q and about the fields checked where all 439 occur (F_3, F_5, F_7); I did not determine for which other fields it holds.

## Open next questions

Structured versions are in `TASK.json`.

1. Is the realizable signature set still the generic census for two planes of three ports (6x6)? First step: enumerate complementary 3-planes of F_2^6 by incidence data. Blocker: the generic 6x6 census has 2^36 supports.
2. Do three planes of two ports admit a signature outside the generic census? #4365's first open question asks for a joint three-plane decoder with 49 closure-pair tariffs, which appear to be the 7 x 7 source and reader masks of three planes. First step: the same enumeration over complementary plane triples in F_2^6. Blocker: 49^6 candidates need symmetry reduction.
3. Which pairs (support of P, support of P^-1) occur? Only a port-level pricing model would see them. Blocker: no such model is written down.

## Related open work

- No open PR studies the plane-level signatures of the two-plane 4x4 interface. None of this account's other open PRs opened since the claim (#6692 to #6696) studies this object.
- #3997 (merged): the source of the question; its generic and signed-ternary censuses give the 439 codes this package matches exactly.
- #3990 (merged): binary screen of the same interface; its 391 binary signatures are a subset of the 439.
- #4365 (merged): proves the invoice floor 8 for arbitrary scalar factorizations. It agrees with the consequence stated here; this PR does not recompute its number.

## CI notes

CI did not certify this head, and the cause is infrastructure, not the package. The `plan` job of the research-packages workflow ([run 41719811223](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41719811223), [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41719811223/job/126209283170)) was cancelled by the workflow's 10-minute timeout while still in its `actions/checkout` step. The job started 21:13:25Z, the checkout step ran 21:13:29Z to 21:23:25Z, and the job completed 21:23:27Z. The `replay` job was skipped. Head: `e68cb25dcc859efb03d616305f543fda2d90ece1`.

Other recent PRs hit the same job. Of the 19 PRs from #6676 to #6696 other than this one that I read, 11 show `plan` cancelled after about 10 minutes with `replay` skipped (#6676 to #6679, #6681 to #6685, #6689, #6692), 6 `plan` jobs succeeded (#6680, #6686, #6687, #6688, #6693, #6694) and 2 were still running (#6695, #6696). I confirmed the cancelled step only for this PR's job.

This result is therefore certified only by the local checks listed under Reproduce: both `verify.py` commands, the registered package replay, the metadata check and the committed-bytes and source-history check. I make no hosted-CI claim, and I have not re-run the workflow or pushed to retrigger it.

## Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. One isolated new package under `research/two-plane-signature-classes/`; no shared code, no change to `upstream/`, no selected-frontier update requested.

**Blast radius:** package-local.
